hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with acute onset severe unilateral pelvic/abdominal pain following activity (intercourse, exercise). May have vaginal bleeding. Exam reveals peritoneal signs, adnexal tenderness, possible palpable mass. Ruptured ovarian cyst → bleeding into peritoneal cavity → hemoperitoneum → hypovolemia and acute abdomen. Most common: ruptured corpus luteum cyst. Differential: ectopic pregnancy (MUST rule out — HCG), PID, appendicitis, ovarian torsion. Diagnosis: HCG negative (rules out ectopic). Transvaginal ultrasound shows free fluid in pelvis/abdomen, ruptured cyst, possible adnexal mass. CBC for anemia from blood loss. Type and screen. Management: stable → observation, analgesia, serial hematocrit. Unstable/hypotensive → IV fluids, blood transfusion if needed, surgical consult (laparoscopy vs laparotomy for hemostasis). If on anticoagulation → reverse.
